sources.title: On local Type I singularities of the Navier-Stokes equations and Liouville theorems
claims_used: Type-I singular behavior is tied to existence of a nontrivial mild bounded ancient solution satisfying the finite-I Type-I condition.
Finite I is defined from scale-critical local A,C,D,E parabolic quantities; stronger global critical controls may imply finite I, but the converse is not supplied by the source.

The compactness step used in the source provides strong L^3_loc convergence of velocity under local integral bounds and weak local pressure convergence; it does not state strong convergence of curl or of the normalized direction field.

sources.title: Logarithmic Depletion of Vortex Stretching and Singularity Evasion in the 3D Navier-Stokes Equations
claims_used: The theorem is conditional on a critical-point singularity profile, including global uniform weak-L^(3/2) vorticity concentration and high-vorticity superlevel localization to a shrinking core.
The vorticity direction is separately assumed uniformly in log-weighted bmo_{1/|log r|}.
The commutator/far-field estimates use the whole-space vorticity through the Biot-Savart/Calderon-Zygmund operator and the global critical Lorentz norm.
The endgame is a regularity criterion for the original finite-time solution near a first possible singular time, not a Liouville theorem for an arbitrary finite-I ancient limit.

expert_cell.finding: The Albritton-Barker producer is deliberately local/scale-critical through finite I. Its compactness theorem gives the velocity convergence needed for the ancient limit but does not itself produce the global Lorentz vorticity amplitude or one-core morphology consumed by the Grujic criterion.
Grujic's L^{3/2,infinity} vorticity hypothesis is precisely a radius-free global distribution control of the kind R7 isolated. R6's O(R) fixed-time capacity cannot be substituted for it.

The direction xi=omega/|omega| is nonlinear and undefined at omega=0. Strong L^3_loc convergence of velocity plus weak derivative information does not by itself yield convergence of xi in the weighted BMO topology; a nonvanishing/strong-vorticity stability lemma would be needed.
Profile decompositions manage translation/dilation only after a global critical norm is available. Importing that machinery before establishing such a state-space bound reverses the implication.

The Grujic commutator uses whole-space Biot-Savart/CZ structure and a global Lorentz source. Albritton-Barker's local pressure localization leaves a harmonic far-field component; no local-pressure estimate here closes the missing whole-space amplitude/tail.

A finite-time regularity criterion for the original flow is not automatically an ancient-solution Liouville theorem. Even if a property held on an ancient limit, lifting it back to the prelimit needs a quantitative stability interface; conversely, if the original Grujic hypotheses hold, the criterion applies directly and the ancient bridge is unnecessary.
Treat the new paper as a conditional consumer, not root evidence. Same-context review has zero independent-review credit. Fail closed on normalized-field convergence and global-tail assumptions.
